based_on: City staff recommend that City Council state its intention to designate the property at 8 Arnold Avenue under Part IV, Section 29 of the Ontario Heritage Act.
The property at 8 Arnold Avenue is located south of Lambton Avenue in the Rockcliffe-Smythe neighbourhood.
The house is a red-brick Ontario Farmhouse-style building from the 1870s or 1880s known as the George Marshall Residence.
The building is the earliest known house in the Mount Dennis community.
On August 19, 2026, Toronto Building received an application to demolish the house at 8 Arnold Avenue.
The property owner must give at least 60 days' written notice to Heritage Planning of their intention to demolish a structure on a listed property.
At the time of the report, the property owner had not yet submitted this notice to Heritage Planning.
Staff found that the property meets three of the nine provincial criteria required for municipal heritage designation.
A property may be designated if it meets two or more of the nine criteria.
Designation allows City Council to review proposed changes or demolitions and enforce heritage maintenance standards.
If there are no objections to the designation, staff recommend that City Council allow the City Solicitor to introduce a bill to designate the property.
